tasks.title: Stop the countdown that never ends
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Timetable.java`, Ossian's countdown prints its first line again and again and never stops. Fix it so it prints one line for each minute, from `minutesToDeparture` down to 1, then `Boarding closed`. Keep the lines it prints as they are.

Check runs your Task 1 lines with countdowns of its own, one of 0 minutes, and reads what they print.
nextSteps: Run `java Timetable.java` and watch the countdown run away. Press Ctrl+C to stop it.
Read the condition of the `while`. What would have to change for it to become false?
Find what changes inside the loop each time round. Today nothing does.
Make the loop move one minute closer to departure each time round, and run again.
hints: A `while` loop runs as long as its condition is true. If nothing inside it changes the condition, it is true forever.
`minutes` should go down by one each time the loop prints a line.
Add `minutes = minutes - 1;` inside the loop, after the line that prints.

tasks.title: Print the day's departures
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, a boat leaves every hour on the hour, from `firstHour` to `lastHour`, both included. With a `for` loop, print one line for each departure:

```
Departs 7:00
```

Check runs your Task 2 lines with days of its own, one with a single departure, and reads every line they print.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about the three parts of a `for` loop.
Decide where the counter starts, the condition that keeps it going, and how it moves.
Print one line inside the loop, built from the counter.
Run it and check the first and the last line against `firstHour` and `lastHour`.
hints: The counter of the loop can be the hour itself, starting at `firstHour`.
"Both included" means the loop must also run when the counter is exactly `lastHour`. Look at which comparison allows equal.
The shape is `for (int hour = firstHour; hour <= lastHour; hour++) { System.out.println(...); }`.

tasks.title: Add up the day's passengers
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, every departure from `firstHour` to `lastHour` carries `rushPassengers` if it leaves before `rushEndsAt`, and `quietPassengers` otherwise. With a loop, make an `int` called `passengersToday`: the passengers of all the day's departures added up.

Check runs your Task 3 lines with days of its own and reads `passengersToday`.
nextSteps: Make `passengersToday` before the loop, starting at 0.
Loop over the hours as in Task 2.
Inside the loop, decide with `if` which number this departure carries, and add it to the total.
Print `passengersToday` after the loop and work out by hand whether it is right.
hints: A running total starts at 0 before the loop, and each time round the loop adds to it.
A variable made inside the loop's braces is made again each time round, and it is gone after the loop. The total has to live outside it.
The shape is `int passengersToday = 0;` then a `for` over the hours with `if (hour < rushEndsAt) { passengersToday = passengersToday + rushPassengers; } else { ... }` inside.

tasks.title: Count the years to the new fare
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, each year the fare goes up by a twentieth of that year's fare, in whole pence: the fare divided by 20, with the part after the point dropped. The rise grows as the fare grows. With a `while` loop, make an `int` called `years`: how many years until the fare reaches `targetPence` or more. A fare that is already there needs 0 years.

Check runs your Task 4 lines with fares of its own, one that lands exactly on the target, and reads `years`.
nextSteps: Make `years` at 0, and a variable for the fare that you can change.
Write the condition that is true while the fare is still below the target.
Inside the loop, raise the fare by a twentieth and count one year.
Print `years` and try a few targets at the top of the file.
hints: A `while` loop is right when you do not know in advance how many times it runs.
Both things must change inside the loop: the fare, so the condition can become false, and `years`, to count. If the fare never changes, the loop never ends.
The shape is `while (fare < targetPence) { fare = fare + fare / 20; years++; }`, with `fare` starting at `farePence`.

tasks.title: Find where the boat's name ends
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 5`, the ticket starts with the boat's name, then a space. Make an `int` called `nameEnd`: the position of the first space in `ticket`, or the length of `ticket` if it has no space. Walk the ticket one position at a time with a loop, and stop it with `break` at the first space.

Check runs your Task 5 lines with tickets of its own, one without a space and one whose boat has two words, reads `nameEnd`, and reads your lines for the loop and the `break`.
nextSteps: Make `nameEnd` with the value it should have if no space is found.
Loop over the positions of `ticket`, from the first to the last.
Inside, look at the character at each position. When it is a space, keep its position and leave the loop.
Print `nameEnd` and try a ticket without a space at the top of the file.
hints: Positions in a `String` run from 0 to one less than its length. `charAt` gives the character at a position, as a `char`, which compares with `==`.
`break` leaves the loop at once. Without it, the loop goes on and a later space would replace the first.
Inside `for (int i = 0; i < ticket.length(); i++)`, write `if (ticket.charAt(i) == ' ') { nameEnd = i; break; }`.
